label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Low, dome-bodied and six-legged-ish, with splayed legs, so the outline roughly matches the brief. But the teeth sit on a separate front piece rather than in a ring, and the top view shows two side spikes that read as horns. Nothing reads as wet. Off in the front and top views.

M2.reason: Measured 28.5 x 26 x 18.2 units, which is headcrab scale. No size was asked (sizeAsked null, sizeOff null), so this rests on the look of the picture against a headcrab, not a number. Pass.

M3.reason: The front view shows dark teeth as scattered spots in a patch, not a ring; the below view shows a short row of spikes on the front piece. Six legs are roughly there (front, side and below views). No separate pale belly part is visible. The teeth and belly are wrong.

M4.reason: The whole body is one mid green, with no pale belly in the below or side views. The brief asks for grey-green with a pale belly. The teeth are dark brown-black, which is close enough. The belly is the clear miss.

M5.reason: Surface detail is flat facets with no wet sheen or wear. The only marks are dark tooth spots in the front view, scattered rather than a ring. The brief asks for wetness and a ring of teeth, so both are missing.

M6.reason: In the line-up, C (ours) is a flat, untextured green blob beside the leech, roach and chumtoad, which are textured and read at once as Half-Life's. A player would not take it for one of the game's. It is clearly off in finish.

M7.reason: The teeth piece faces forward in the left and front views, the body stands on its legs and is upright, and the pose holds in the side views. Nothing in the brief fixes an origin, so this is judged on the look of the stance.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors, and 428 triangles is well under twice the median of Half-Life's creatures of this size (those run well above 1,000), so the count is not a problem. Nothing is visibly open or floating in the stills.

C1.reason: In attack.png (labelled JUMP, not ATTACK, so it is not the attack the brief asks for) the front piece looks detached: at frames 9, 13, 17 and 21 of 30 it floats above the body with a gap and the legs do not visibly join it. The run in run.png holds together and the legs stay on the floor line. The jump is the failure.

C2.reason: The harness reports the contract as kept (the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts), so the game's own headcrab plays it. Measured by compareContract, as the rubric asks, and it holds.
